newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle pilots reject tentative pact.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle pilots reject tentative pact.

text.p: The pilots at AMR Corp's American Eagle division Monday rejected a contract proposal that would have covered all 1,900 pilots flying for the four regional carriers operating under the Eagle name, the pilots union said.
The union said 642 pilots opposed the tentative agreement, while 505 pilots voted in favour. American Eagle and the union reached a tentative contract in May.
"The airline will continue negotiations with its pilots union, the Air Line Pilots Association," an American Eagle statement said.
"We're disappointed," said Capt. Homer Pugh, chairman of the pilot group's master executive council, which had endorsed the agreement in June.

"It was a complicated contract, and, in that type of situation, there is probably no simple explanation of today's count. But if we can pinpoint the areas of concern, I believe we can refine our strategy and ultimately reach an agreement that our members can support," Pugh said.
Terms of the tentative contract were not disclosed.

The contract rejection follows a similar move in January by the pilots of AMR Corp.'s larger airline unit, American Airlines. The American Airlines pilots voted against a labour agreement even though it had been endorsed by their union leaders. The American pilots and the airline eventually reached a labour agreement after months of bitter negotiations that included a brief strike and intervention by President Clinton.
The American Eagle pilot leaders said they will now meet to assess the factors which may have contributed to the contract's rejection, and to determine their next course of action.

The rejected American Eagle contract would have provided for a single contract covering the four wholly owned operating carriers that fly as American Eagle: Simmons Airlines, Flagship Airlines, Executive Airlines and Wings West.
The four carriers won the right to bargain as a unit for representational purposes in August 1995.
American Eagle is the world's largest regional airline system, operating more than 1,400 daily flights to 125 cities throughout the United States, Canada, the Bahamas and the Caribbean.
All four of its affiliate carriers are owned by AMR Eagle Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of AMR Corp.
